source.title: Analysis of Generalizability of Deep Neural Networks Based on the Complexity of Decision Boundary

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different measured property—decision-boundary complexity—tracks test accuracy among trained networks with similarly high training accuracy.
record.gate_note: The study reports decision-boundary complexity scores and test accuracies for trained models. It has no results on the claim versions’ named interventions or measurements; synthetic-data models have no test data.
record.test_reason: The cats-and-dogs experiment compares two convolutional classifiers with a fully connected classifier: cC1 and cC2 achieve test accuracies of 0.730 and 0.626, versus 0.583 for cC3. This bears on V3 in a new image setting, although the extracted rows measure DBC rather than the architectural accuracy comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that smaller DBC identifies simpler boundaries and better generalizability among models trained on the same dataset. They restrict comparisons to the same dataset and acknowledge that a smaller local DBC is insufficient to establish a simpler boundary.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a decision-boundary-complexity measure based on entropy of eigenvalues from adversarial examples; it does not test the listed versions’ methods.
record.method_sensitivity: For the cats-and-dogs models, the authors report the ordering cC1 < cC2 < cC3 for DBC across all tested neighbor counts (3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30).

fits_no_version.finding: Lower local DBC accompanies higher test accuracy across the two breast-cancer models and three cats-and-dogs models. The cats-and-dogs ordering persists across all six tested neighbor counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local decision-boundary complexity measured through eigenvalue entropy of boundary samples tracks test accuracy among models trained on the same dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
record.problems: Only two datasets provide paired DBC and test-accuracy results; DBC is reported as a proxy and the authors state it is meaningless for a single model and cannot be compared across datasets. For the breast-cancer scores, the authors report no standard deviations because the distributions are non-Gaussian and long-tailed.
record.rows_left_out: The synthetic 2-D experiment is omitted because the text says there are no test data, so it does not report a train–test generalization result. Cats-and-dogs DBC results across the other neighbor counts are shown in Figure 8 without exact values; the table’s 15-nearest-neighbor results are extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
A width sweep past interpolation with other architectural and training choices held fixed.

The contribution of local connectivity specifically; learned sparse connectivity; initialization from a trained convolutional network; the named benchmark datasets. Optimizer and initialization details are not supplied.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
The effect of adding or removing dropout with architecture held fixed. Dropout co-varies with architectural differences here.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness, its relationship to generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Separate test-accuracy rows for cC1 (0.730), cC2 (0.626), and cC3 (0.583), with cC3 as the fully connected baseline. Record the architectural differences: cC1 has three convolutional layers, pooling, a 64-neuron dense layer and dropout; cC2 has one convolutional layer and three dense layers; cC3 has only a 1,024-neuron dense layer. All have reported training accuracy above 0.95.
missing.locator: Section III.C, Figure 7 caption and Table II

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the architectural comparison embedded in the cats-and-dogs experiment. DBC measures boundary geometry in input space, not V7's sensitivity to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations. The synthetic experiment has no held-out data. The E1 support sentence miscopies the source: Section III.B states that bC2 has larger local DBC scores than bC1.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparative test error of convolutional and fully connected networks, including learned or transferred connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch performance under fixed or adapted training recipes.
Effects of dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.reason: Based on Figure 7 and Table II, pending missing accuracy rows: convolutional cC1 and cC2 score 0.730 and 0.626 versus fully connected cC3's 0.583. Depth, size and dropout also differ, so the comparison does not isolate local connectivity.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher accuracy of cC1 and cC2 over fully connected cC3 remains unverified amid architecture and dropout differences.
